title: deploy with docker example show wrong arguments
description:
In the following link, https://vetiver.rstudio.com/learn-more/deploy-with-docker.html#create-docker-artifacts, the code reads as follows:

```r
vetiver_prepare_docker(board, "julia.silge/superbowl_rf", port = 8080)
```

But `vetiver_prepare_docker()` does't have a `port` argument https://rstudio.github.io/vetiver-r/dev/reference/vetiver_prepare_docker.html. The same intention appears to be fulfilled using the `docker_args` argument

```r
vetiver_prepare_docker(board, "julia.silge/superbowl_rf", docker_args = list(port = 8000))
```

title: Why do we need VetiverAPI and VetiverModel?
description:
From a vetiver user: 
> Would you ever consider allowing `VetiverAPI` without `VetiverModel`?

In an MLOps best practices world, you should version each experiment and then choose one of the models to deploy, and `VetiverModel` is more easily versioned/reasoned about than the API as a whole, especially if people have custom metadata for the model they want to track.

It might be useful to add some documentation around this question somewhere.

title: Document that folder pin boards are not automatically compatible with Docker
description:
Follow up of: https://github.com/rstudio/vetiver-r/issues/211

Folder based pin boards are not immediately available in a Docker images. They can be made available by either copying the folder into the Docker container or mounting a volume. 

It would be beneficial to note this in the [Deploy with Docker article](https://vetiver.rstudio.com/learn-more/deploy-with-docker.html).

title: Add more details about vetiver.load_pkgs()...
description:
Hi,

I tried with several different alternatives how to use `vetiver.load_pkgs() to generate a vetiver_requirements.txt` and then build a Docker, but I get constant errors.

Please could you expand the documentation for that function.

I tried these alternatives:

```python
from vetiver import load_pkgs

load_pkgs()
load_pkgs(model_board)
load_pkgs(app_file)
```
And they produced several kind of erorrs...

The only one that worked was:

```python
from vetiver import load_pkgs

load_pkgs(v)
```
It run but generated this message  `pip-compile: command not found` and there is no new file the `vetiver_requirements.txt`.

Thanks a lot for **vetiver** it makes really easy how to expose and deploy a model!
Carlos.

Thanks,
Carlos.

title: clarify RStudio Connect integration
description:
In the "Deploy" section, we say:

> FastAPI and Plumber APIs such as these can be hosted in a variety of ways. You can create a ready-to-go file for deployment that is especially suited for [RStudio Connect](https://www.rstudio.com/products/connect/).

however, for `vetiver./_deploy_rsconnect`, you don't need to create this file. This sentence is a bit misleading, as it looks like you need to create a FastAPI/Plumber API file to deploy to Connect. We probably need to reword this and/or add in explanation of the function `deploy_rsconnect`.

title: Add $model output to data.txt file
description:
The output of $model for a vetiver model seems useful to keep when using vetiver_pin_write(board) i.e.

```

  workflow(mpg ~ ., linear_reg()) %>%
  fit(mtcars)


v <- vetiver_model(car_mod, "cars_lr")

```

title: Use `aria-label` YAML when using icon links
description:
Undersung hero (parameter/option) is that you can actually add an `aria-label` to the icon links:
https://github.com/juliasilge/vetiver.dev/blob/4424dadcf46e5a1cf9bf40784ebe4dc6b31c3381/_quarto.yml#L23-L24

So, for example, in the Quarto website `_quarto.yml` I added:
```
    right:
      - icon: twitter
        href: https://twitter.com/quarto_pub
        aria-label: Quarto Twitter
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli
        aria-label: Quarto GitHub
```

For when those two are used in the navbar and footer. (Again, I can put in a PR for this)
